title: The Morning Brief: A memorial, a comeback bid, and a card-industry lawsuit deepen
dek: The desk's morning stories span a legal escalation between the two dominant trading card companies, the death of a college baseball icon, and injury-return progress for Shohei Ohtani.
author: GoCheckMySports
key_fact: The Panini-Fanatics card licensing case has moved from broad antitrust claims to specific allegations of trade secret misuse, a shift that will play out in discovery over the coming months.
bottom_line: The day's defining story is legal: newly unsealed filings show Panini accusing Fanatics of using its confidential licensing data, down to specific royalty rates and spend obligations, to win exclusive NBA and NFL card deals, escalating a three-year antitrust case beyond general competitive claims. Alongside that, college baseball marked the death of Skip Bertman at 88, the coach who built LSU into a five-time national champion, while the Dodgers reported encouraging progress in Shohei Ohtani's return from knee injury after a 35-pitch bullpen session. The honest read on the Panini filing is that the allegations are now specific but the mechanism by which any information changed hands is not detailed in what has been unsealed. Coming checkpoints include discovery and any summary judgment ruling in the card licensing case, Ohtani's next bullpen session in the two-to-five-day window the Dodgers outlined, and the start of France's Nations League fixtures in September under Zidane's new staff.
body: The day's most consequential story is legal rather than competitive: newly unsealed court filings show Panini now accusing Fanatics of obtaining and using its confidential licensing data, including royalty rates, minimum guarantee schedules, marketing commitments, and autograph spend obligations, to win exclusive trading card deals with the NBA, NFL, and their players unions. A magistrate judge unsealed the allegations this week over Fanatics' objection, in a case Panini has pursued for three years.

Elsewhere, the day carries a mix of loss, progress, and roster building. LSU baseball is remembering Skip Bertman, who died Friday at 88 after building the program into a five-time national champion during his tenure as coach, then later serving as athletic director during LSU football's national championship runs in 2003 and 2007. In Los Angeles, Shohei Ohtani threw a 35-pitch bullpen session Friday, his first mound work in more than three weeks since a July 3 left knee injury, with manager Dave Roberts describing the step as encouraging. In international soccer, new France coach Zinedine Zidane appointed Fabien Barthez, his 1998 World Cup and 2000 European Championship teammate, as goalkeeper coach. And in rugby, Australia beat Japan 56-17 in Townsville, its third straight Test win under coach Les Kiss, after trailing at halftime before pulling away on set piece and breakdown strength.

The throughline connecting the Panini filing to the rest of the day is less about final scores and more about institutions in transition: a legal fight over who controls a multibillion-dollar card licensing market, a coaching legacy closing out, a two-way star mapping a path back to competition, and a new national team staff taking shape.

On the why: the reporting on Panini's allegations does not detail how the confidential information allegedly moved from Panini to Fanatics, only that Panini now claims the information was obtained and used. That gap is central to what comes next in the case. Ohtani's return path is more mechanical than mysterious: the club has laid out a stepwise plan of bullpen sessions followed by live batting practice, and Roberts framed Friday's outing as one data point in that sequence. Zidane's appointment of Barthez reflects an evident preference for figures from France's championship era as he assembles his staff, though the story does not elaborate on selection criteria beyond that pairing. Australia's second-half turnaround against Japan is attributed specifically to set piece and breakdown dominance after a shaky first half, per the day's report.
Desk boards were not available this cycle, so today's figures rest entirely on the sourced stories themselves.

In the Panini-Fanatics case, watch for discovery developments that could show the specific route the disputed information allegedly took, and whether Fanatics' summary judgment motion succeeds in narrowing or dismissing the fraud claims before any trial. For Ohtani, the next checkpoint is another bullpen session in the two-to-five-day window Roberts outlined, which would need to pass without setback before live batting practice becomes the next test. France's coaching staff and goalkeeper preparation will next be visible when Nations League fixtures begin in September, and Australia's second-half pattern under Kiss will be tested again in the Nations Championship.
